newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, outperform U.S. issues. [CORRECTED 01:19 GMT 22/1]
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, outperform U.S. issues. [CORRECTED 01:19 GMT 22/1]

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing (corrects from widening) as markets enjoyed a sense of relief following testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, analysts said.

"The thing that drove the market's tone generally was Greenspan's comments," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "There was a lot of fear heading into that, and this is mostly a sense of relief in the bond markets."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.75 to C$109.00 to yield 7.230 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 16/32 to yield 6.79 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 44 basis points from 48 basis points at Monday's close.

Canadian bonds had weakened with U.S. issues in early trade on concerns Greenspan's comments could spark a selloff. However Greenspan's testimony that inflation remains in check despite a vigorous U.S. economy prompted many investors to cover short positions.
Canadian bonds strengthened amid the rebound in U.S. Treasury prices. Dealers said spreads to U.S. bonds may have narrowed in part because of recent Canadian dollar strength.
Canadian bond investors are also looking ahead to the auction on Wednesday of C$1.3 billion 30-year Government of Canada bonds, analysts said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.55 to C$103.40 to yield 6.525 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to one basis point from six basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.81 percent against the U.S. bill which last yielded 5.17 percent.
